The test `test_contains_na_dtype` checks whether `CategoricalIndex` correctly handles NaT (`Not a Time`) values when it contains datetime data. The error occurred because the assert statement `assert np.timedelta64("NaT") not in obj` failed, indicating that there was an unexpected NaT value present in the `obj` which is supposed to be a CategoricalIndex.

The bug lies within the `__init__` method of the `CategoricalIndex` class where it doesn't handle NaT values correctly while creating the index. This allows an unwanted NaT timedelta64 object to exist in our categorical index, causing our assertion to fail.

Conclusion: The test `test_contains_na_dtype` checks whether CategoricalIndex handles NaT datetime values correctly but failed because the `__init__` method of CategoricalIndex does not handle NaT values properly, leading to an unexpected NaT timedelta64 object in the index.
